payload.chart:
SECOND FILL. The chart is re-run rather than edited, because C5's definition changed and C9 did not exist when the first chart was pruned — and a chart pruned under a wrong criterion cannot be repaired by adding a row.

STATE-OF-THE-ART SCAN FOR ARCHITECTURES, run here as this state's guidance requires: agent-harness tool surfaces (a file lane plus a search lane plus a shell lane, with the search lane wrapping a fast external searcher rather than implementing one); editor architectures, which is where the packaged-searcher pattern comes from; version-control-as-database, where history is queried in place rather than exported; and formal review practice, where the review is an ENTRY AND EXIT contract on a work product rather than a separate activity. Two of the four changed a row below, and both are named where they did.

ROW 1 — SEARCH THE WORKING TREE (F1, K1)
  (a) hand-rolled scanner in our own language. PRUNED. It exists today, and C9 is decisive rather than advisory: it lost on every axis it was measured on and produced the four-calls-for-one-answer cost that R3 records. Deleted by C5, since it answers the same question as (b).
  (b) packaged fast searcher, resolved through the dependency rather than the PATH. KEPT.
  (c) version-control grep over the working tree. KEPT AS A ROW-1 OPTION but see the pruning note below.
  (d) system-installed fast searcher on the PATH. PRUNED by probe P1 — not present on the owner's own machine, so this is not an option, it is a hope.

ROW 2 — SEARCH THE RECORD (F4, K1)
  (a) version-control grep over refs. KEPT. Probe P2: works, and returns parseable ref:path:line form.
  (b) check a ref out to a temporary tree, then run the fast searcher. PRUNED — pays a working-tree materialisation for every historical question, and C6 bounds cost.
  (c) build an index of shipped evidence. PRUNED by C1 — an index tolerates staleness, and worse, it is a THIRD thing to keep correct.
  (d) do not search the record. PRUNED by C2, which is a veto.

THE ROW 1 / ROW 2 PRUNING NOTE, and it is the correction this whole rewalk exists to carry. The first pass collapsed these two rows into one and chose 1(c)+2(a) — version control for everything — on the reading that two search tools violate C5. That reading was wrong, and the owner said so: 'this is not one job, it's two jobs.' Applying C5's REWRITTEN test — name the question both paths answer — Row 1 asks 'what is in the bytes on disk right now, including files version control has never seen', and Row 2 asks 'what did a shipped revision say'. Different questions, different answers, and one tool cannot answer both well: version-control grep cannot see an untracked file, which is precisely the state of every file an agent has just created. C5 therefore DOES NOT APPLY ACROSS the two rows. It still applies WITHIN each row, and it deletes the hand-rolled scanner.
C9 confirms independently: the day this decision was first made produced four measured failures, and the design that ignored the working-tree/history distinction was one of them.

ROW 3 — DELIVER A PORTION (F2)
  (a) read the file and slice by line range. KEPT.
  (b) render a revision and slice. KEPT for the ref case only — it is the same job answered in the other row's context, not a competitor.

ROW 4 — REACH OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY (F3)
  (a) declared names resolved through machine-local settings; the record carries the name, the settings carry the path. KEPT.
  (b) absolute paths in the record. PRUNED — unauditable, and it puts a machine's layout into a shared record.
  (c) submodules. PRUNED — changes the repository's shape for a read-only need.

ROW 5 — SELECT THE RULES THAT BIND A STATE (F14, K4)
  (a) machine-readable applicability — state ids, state kinds, or tags — plus migration of the ten existing nodes. KEPT.
  (b) each state declares the rules it carries. PRUNED ON SIGHT: that is exactly the hand-wiring whose absence caused the problem, and it fails the moment a rule is minted after the state was authored, which is the whole scenario.
  (c) semantic match of a rule's prose against the state's statement. KEPT AS A CONTENDER, and only with an M5 spike, because 'does it pick the RIGHT rules' is a claim to be measured, not asserted — C7 is weight 5 and a plausible-but-wrong rule costs attention while looking like coverage.
  (d) (a) plus a report of every rule that declares no applicability. KEPT — it is (a) with F29 attached, and R37 requires F29 regardless.

ROW 6 — COLLECT THE REVIEW (F32, K7)
  (a) inject the rounds at the single place evidence forms are built. KEPT.
  (b) author the rounds into each gate by hand. PRUNED by C5 and by history — it is one edit per gate forever, and a gate authored later simply misses them. This is how the rounds came to be required-but-never-collected in the first place.
  (c) a separate review sub-machine per gate. PRUNED for this iteration — it changes the machine's shape, which the excluded list rules out. Recorded as the natural successor if entry criteria are ever added, since that is where the review-as-contract pattern from the scan would land.
  (d) a lint that complains after a gate passed. PRUNED — it detects the omission instead of preventing it, and an unattended run has already moved on.

ROW 7 — RETURN WORK TO AN EARLIER POINT (F33 + F34, K7)
  (a) reopen in the machine core: re-activate the named states and their cone, supersede prior fills, and RE-ARM the joins fed from outside the cone. KEPT.
  (b) abandon the iteration and restart it. PRUNED — it destroys the record of what was believed, which is the one thing a reopen is for.
  (c) edit the instance by hand. PRUNED by C5 and C9 — it is an out-of-lane write, and this iteration has already paid for one.
  NOTE, from C9: option (a) MINUS the re-arm is not a cheaper variant, it is the deadlock this project observed today. The chart records it as a single option deliberately, so no candidate can pick half of it.

ROW 8 — DELIVER THE SHARED JUDGE (F36, K8)
  (a) promote engine files to trunk under discipline: trunk current, engine files only, whole suite green in trunk, all-or-nothing. KEPT.
  (b) each worktree runs its own engine. PRUNED — two parallel agents would then be judged by different machines and a gate stops meaning one thing. This is the tension T2 the partitioning names.
  (c) wait for the close. PRUNED by C9 — measured at six declared workarounds in one day.
  (d) a shared engine directory outside version control. PRUNED — unversioned, so no revision, no review, no way back.

ROW 9 — DECIDE MECHANICALLY (K5)
  (a) a lint registry whose every check yields pass, fail or defer-with-reason. KEPT.
  (b) checks written inline in each gate. PRUNED by C5.
  (c) an external linter over the record. PRUNED — it cannot see run results or evidence, which is most of what the checks need.

ROW 10 — KEEP THE RECORD REACHABLE (K6)
  (a) annotated tags, the commit hash recorded in the grant, and the branch deleted after the merge. KEPT.
  (b) tags only. PRUNED by probe P3 — observed ambiguity between a branch and a tag of the same name.
  (c) copy every iteration's evidence into the working tree. PRUNED — it undoes the close-and-merge split deliberately made earlier.
payload.shortlist:
THREE COMBINATIONS SEEDED. All three share Rows 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 — those rows have one surviving option each and pretending otherwise would be decision theatre. The candidates differ ONLY where a real choice remains: how the working tree and the record are searched, and how rules are selected.

X1 — FIT PER JOB (Row 1b + Row 2a + Row 5d)
A packaged fast searcher answers the working tree; version-control grep answers the record; rules are selected by machine-readable applicability plus a report of every unattached rule. Two searchers because there are two questions; the hand-rolled scanner is deleted. This is the combination the first pass rejected under the mis-defined C5.

X2 — ONE SEARCHER (Row 1c + Row 2a + Row 5d)
Version-control grep answers both the working tree and the record; rules as in X1. One search mechanism, one code path, and the dependency disappears. This is the first pass's choice, kept as a real candidate rather than a straw man — it is genuinely simpler, and its cost must be stated rather than assumed.

X3 — FIT PER JOB, RULES BY MEANING (Row 1b + Row 2a + Row 5c)
Searching as X1; rules selected by semantic match against the state's statement instead of by declared applicability. Cheapest migration by far, since the ten existing nodes need no rewriting and nothing must be authored going forward — and it rests entirely on a claim about selection quality that has never been measured here. Carried to the spike, not past it.
